calls.text: Base case: $0.081 per PAPER by Oct 2027 (Version 2: $0.11; Version 3: $0.034; Version 4: $0.014; Version 5: $0.0094; Version 6: $0.015; Version 7: $0.00070)

history.evidence: The call as made.
Revenue and the stakers' share are both above the base inputs; re-run on 17 Oct the same method gives $0.11. Nothing resolves before mid-November.

First tell, logged at 10:47 UTC: the house pool slipped under the $5M bar ($4.83M), so stakers have had only the 1% win fee since about midnight UTC. One quiet Saturday is not new evidence; 16 Oct closed at $5.45M of revenue, above the $4.45M Version 1 started from. If stakers' share is still under 80% on 28 Oct, the base-case refill date, the base case comes down in the next version.

Off track on the desk's own number: re-run on 20 Oct the same method gives $0.034, under the $0.081 called, because the reference fell 73% ($6.29M to $1.72M a day on 17–19 Oct) and the market's median bet fell from $200M to $25M. Not dead: $1.72M a day is still 3.9× what the base case needs after the rush ($0.45M in Version 1's frame). Resolves Oct 2027.

Re-run on 27 Oct gives $0.014 against the $0.081 called: the three-day reference fell another 60% ($1.72M to $0.68M a day on 24–26 Oct), and the new mint rule live since 21 Oct adds supply with no ceiling (−7% on its own). Revenue over the last seven days, $0.77M a day, is still 1.7× what Version 1's base case needs after the rush ($0.44M). Resolves Oct 2027.

Re-run on 10 Nov gives $0.0094 against the $0.081 called: the three-day reference fell another 36% ($0.68M to $0.44M a day on 7–9 Nov); the share to stakers (97%) and supply barely moved it. Against Version 1's fixed bars, the last seven days ($0.47M a day) sit right at the base case's $0.44M.

Re-run on 11 Nov gives $0.015 against the $0.081 called (Version 5: $0.0094). The rise is one day: 10 Nov's $1.00M replaced 7 Nov's $60K in the three-day reference (+72%). Against Version 1's fixed bars the last seven days ($0.59M a day) sit nearest base, 1.3× its $0.44M bar.

Re-run on 17 Nov gives $0.00070 against the $0.081 called (Version 6: $0.015). The three-day reference fell 92% (14–16 Nov: $90K, $56K, $31K) and stakers' share fell to 51%, both because the pool sat under the bar after a $2.14M win on 13 Nov. With both inputs over seven days the base would be $0.0085. Against Version 1's fixed bars, the last seven days ($0.42M a day) sit nearest base, 0.94× its $0.44M bar.

history.evidence: The call as made: the restart date tells the case.
At today's $6.3M a day the pool refills in about a day, so the first reading will likely say bull without separating the cases. The reading that counts comes after the rush fades.

Tell at 10:47 UTC: the pool is under the $5M bar before it doubles tonight, so the refill to $10M starts from $4.83M, about $5.2M of net losses. Stakers' income has been near zero since midnight UTC ($20K between 04:46 and 10:47 against $51.2M all time). Traders are ahead $1.0M on open trades; Bitcoin flat at $81.5K. Each case's date stands; the data marks the restart itself.

PaperDash's daily allocation to stakers agrees with DefiLlama's holders line to the dollar ($0.78M, $2.12M, $1.69M on 17–19 Oct), so the dollars are real; the ratio is the wrong test. Left as the rule scored it; the fix (a pool-at-the-bar rule on the contract read) is lined up for Insaaf.

calls.text: Mint rate falls under 10 PAPER per $1: bull ~14 Nov, base ~29 Jan 2027

history.evidence: The call as made.
Running early: the live contract puts the rate at ~12 per $1 on 17 Oct (16.6 reported on 16 Oct).

10.3 PAPER per $1 on the 20 Oct contract read (high-water mark $254M; the rate crosses under 10 at $259.5M). At the current pace it crosses within about a day, three weeks ahead of the bull date, for the same reason the stop line came early: the curve runs on gross flow. The page marks it from the daily read.

Marked itself hit on the 21 Oct contract read: 9.93 PAPER per $1 once the old curve's high-water mark passed $259.5M ($260.7M), about three weeks before the bull date. Hours later, at 22:00 UTC, the upgrade retired that curve: each $1 lost now mints a fixed share of supply, 9.80 per $1 at the switch and 9.94 today, rising as supply grows, so it passes 10 again at 9.08B. The hit stands as scored; the call's premise (a falling rate) no longer holds.

Stands: it marked itself hit on the 21 Oct read on the old curve. Under the new rule the rate is supply × c and rises with supply: 10.04 on 30 Oct, 10.22 on 10 Nov (9.28B PAPER). The job's mint_rate field still prints the retired curve's 9.80 (BOARD 25).

Stands: it marked itself hit on the 21 Oct read on the old curve. Under the new rule the rate is supply × c and rises with supply: 10.24 PAPER per $1 on 11 Nov (9.305B PAPER). The job's mint_rate field still prints the retired curve's 9.80 (BOARD 25).

Stands: it marked itself hit on the 21 Oct read on the old curve. Under the live rule the rate is supply × c and rises with supply: 10.36 PAPER per $1 on 17 Nov (9.407B PAPER). From the 17 Nov row the job's mint_rate field computes the live rule (BOARD 25); earlier rows keep the retired curve's value.
